city_center.name: Milwaukee Public Market (Historic Third Ward) + Lake Michigan lakefront
city_center.landmark: Milwaukee Public Market in the Third Ward; cream-city brick buildings; Lake Michigan lakefront; Door County cherry country to the north
city_center.notes: Milwaukee is built of pale 'cream city' brick, a local yellow-buff clay brick that defines its historic streetscape. The Milwaukee Public Market anchors the Third Ward. Door County, north up the Lake Michigan shore, is Wisconsin's cherry country. sources: en.wikipedia.org Cream City brick; milwaukeepublicmarket.org.

cultural_notes: Milwaukee's historic buildings are made of pale 'cream city' brick, a local yellow-buff clay brick that is a defining architectural identity (source: Cream City brick, en.wikipedia.org)
Door County, up the Lake Michigan shore, is Wisconsin's cherry country -- tart cherries peak in July and are a signature state crop (source: Door County cherry growers framing, publicly documented)
German and Polish heritage anchor Milwaukee's food culture; a large Mexican community on the near South Side adds to the mix (source: general demographic framing, publicly documented)
Wisconsin is America's Dairyland -- cheese supports savory Power Cakes ties; Pick 'n Save, Meijer, and Metro Market are the grocers (source: chain regional footprint; Wisconsin dairy framing)
